desc:
Decide whether the whole string s is matched by the pattern p. The pattern may contain lowercase letters and two special characters:

  • ? matches exactly one arbitrary character.
  • * matches any sequence of characters, including the empty sequence.

The match must cover the entire string, not just a part of it. For example, s = "adceb" matches p = "*a*b", and s = "acdcb" does not match p = "a*c?b".
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
p consists of lowercase English letters, '?' and '*'
hints: Try a dynamic programme over prefixes: dp[i][j] says whether s[:i] matches p[:j]. Work out the transition for a letter, for ?, and for *.
A star can be either empty (dp[i][j-1]) or consume one more character (dp[i-1][j]). That gives an O(n · m) table; can you do better on memory?

Greedy alternative: remember the position of the most recent * and the text index it currently covers up to. On a mismatch, extend that star by one more character and retry the pattern after it. Only the latest star ever needs revisiting.
editorial: Dynamic programming: let dp[i][j] be true when the first i characters of s match the first j of p. Base case dp[0][0] = true, and dp[0][j] is true only while the pattern prefix consists of stars. For a letter or ?, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] when the characters are compatible. For a star, dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] or dp[i-1][j]. Rolling rows reduce space to O(m); time is O(n · m).

A tighter greedy exists because stars are so permissive. Walk through s and p with two pointers. When p[j] is a letter equal to s[i] or a ?, advance both. When it is a star, record star = j and mark = i, and advance only j (the star starts by matching nothing). On a mismatch with a recorded star, return to star + 1 and let the star swallow one more character: mark += 1; i = mark. A mismatch without a star means no match.

Why only the last star matters: everything before the last star is already matched in the cheapest possible way, and by earlier choices the later star can absorb whatever is needed, so any assignment that works for an earlier star can be shifted onto the latest one. After the text is consumed, the remaining pattern must be only stars. The greedy is O(n · m) in the worst case but O(n + m) on typical inputs and uses O(1) extra space.
